findings.evidence: no visible focus indicator (outline: none 3px rgb(255, 255, 255))
findings.after: Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid; outline-offset: 2px } in a colour at 3:1 against the ground.
findings.title: Visible focus everywhere
findings.fix: Use :focus-visible with a 2px ring offset 2px in a contrasting colour.

findings.evidence: page is 1024px wide at a 375px viewport (sideways scroll); widest culprit 1024px
findings.title: No horizontal overflow
findings.fix: Find the overflowing element; use min-width: 0, overflow-wrap, and avoid 100vw.

findings.evidence: Out of context 'Learn more' names no subject or destination; it jumps to 'Sample information section'.
findings.after: How [product] collects design feedback [DATA NEEDED: product name]
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context): the surrounding text gives no context either.
findings.title: Every control has an accessible name

findings.where: three hero links styled as buttons
findings.evidence: Links with in-page hrefs (#start, #demo, #learn) are drawn as filled buttons; after activation focus stays on the link because the target sections have no tabindex="-1", so keyboard and screen-reader users are not moved to the section they chose in all browsers.
findings.after: <section id="start" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="start-h"> so the in-page jump moves focus
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 Focus Order and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (section labelled by its heading, A11-104).
findings.title: Prefer native controls

findings.evidence: "The future of better workflows." Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: true for Figma, Notion, Asana or any SaaS. Failed T-THREE-LINE: not picturable, not falsifiable, not only-this-business. Failed T-FIVE-SECOND: the product is never named, nor who it is for.
findings.after: Name the job of the design feedback tool in concrete terms, e.g. 'Comments pinned to the exact pixel, from review to fix' [DATA NEEDED: product name and its one specific capability]
findings.why: A headline that fits every company is the clearest single sign of a default page.
findings.title: Swap / rival's-name test: any head still true with a competitor's name (or the same trade

findings.where: CTA row: Get started / Book a demo / Learn more
findings.evidence: Three identical slate buttons of equal weight offer three competing next steps; 'Learn more' is the stock secondary label (L4). Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: this exact trio is the agent default for a SaaS hero.
findings.before: [Get started] [Book a demo] [Learn more] all same fill
findings.after: One primary action styled as primary (e.g. 'Try it on a Figma file' [DATA NEEDED: real first step]); at most one quieter text link for the demo; delete 'Learn more'
findings.why: Equal-weight CTAs mean no decision was made about what the visitor should do (SLP-223).
findings.title: Ban a stock second action beside the hero primary ("Learn more", "See how it works", "Watc

findings.where: html > body > main > p:nth-of-type(3)  "Powerful. Seamless. Innovative."
findings.title: No slop diction
findings.fix: Replace with a specific claim only this business can make, or delete.

findings.evidence: "Powerful. Seamless. Innovative." Three virtue adjectives as fragments (SLP-233 choppy fragments, SLP-220 list of three with nothing to list). Failed T-FRESH-READER: the most generic line on the page.
findings.after: One sentence that says who uses it and what changes for them [DATA NEEDED: target user and measured outcome]
findings.why: Adjective triplets are filler that claim quality without evidence.
findings.title: Ban stock phrases and filler openers (L2).

findings.evidence: "DESIGN FEEDBACK TOOL" in caps above the headline. T-EYEBROW: covering it loses the only words that say what the product is, which shows the information belongs in the headline, not in a label.
findings.before: DESIGN FEEDBACK TOOL / The future of better workflows.
findings.after: Promote it into the h1: '[Product name] is a design feedback tool for …' [DATA NEEDED: product name, audience]
findings.why: The eyebrow carries the page's only fact while the headline carries none.
findings.title: Ban the eyebrow: short inert type before a heading that only announces it, in any geometry

findings.evidence: "Sample start section", "Sample demo section", "Sample information section" with one-line bodies; each is a placeholder anchor target for a hero button. Failed T-DELETION: removing them loses no product information.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real sections: how the tool works on a real file, pricing, who uses it]
findings.title: Ban category-label section heads ("Features", "Our story", "Why us", "How it works"), "Mee

findings.where: html > body > main > p.note:nth-of-type(1)  "Intentionally weak fictional example. Included as "
findings.evidence: 92-character run at 15px (hard floor 12px, dense UI 14px, body 16px)
findings.title: Text size floors
findings.fix: Raise to the floor; cut words rather than shrink.

findings.evidence: The capitals are in the source text (text-transform: none), so some screen readers spell 'DESIGN' or read it with shouting emphasis.
findings.after:
Design feedback tool

with text-transform: uppercase in CSS if caps are kept
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (presentation in content).
findings.title: Keep all words as real text in reading order

findings.evidence: Only a <main> landmark exists (no header, nav or footer), and the hero is not wrapped in a header or section, so the product label, h1 and CTAs share one undifferentiated region with the notice banner.
findings.after: <header> for the hero; move the notice into a role="note" element outside the hero
findings.title: Use landmarks and semantic elements
